# M7: Hardening, reviews and go-live

Goal: prove the app is correct, safe and pleasant on real phones. No new features.

## Steps
1. **Coverage gaps:** list every SPEC section and CURRICULUM section in a table in `NOTES.md`
   with the test(s) that cover it. Add tests for anything uncovered.
2. **Mutation checks** (STANDARDS §3). Break each, confirm a test fails, restore
   (`git checkout -- <file>`), confirm green. Record each result in `NOTES.md`:
   1. `validate.ts`: accept non-integer xp in strict mode;
   2. `backup.ts`: remove the 1 MB size check;
   3. `store.ts`: remove the rev-conflict re-apply;
   4. `store.ts`: write the empty document when stored data is unreadable;
   5. `store.ts`: skip strict validation before writing;
   6. `geometry.ts`: drop the last ledger line;
   7. `srs.ts`: wrong answer → `box - 1` instead of `box - 2`;
   8. `lessonBuilder.ts`: remove the consecutive-duplicate repair;
   9. `session.ts`: allow a second retry of the same question;
   10. `curriculum.ts`: delete one lesson (lock test must fail);
   11. `vite.config.ts`: remove the CSP plugin (check-dist and e2e must fail);
   12. `planners.ts`: checkpoint completes all units 1–10 regardless of `completesUnits`.
3. **Accessibility pass:** keyboard-only run through a lesson on desktop (Tab/Enter/Space work
   everywhere, focus visible, Sheets trap and return focus); `aria-live` feedback; every button
   has a name (Playwright `getByRole` finds them); reduced motion; 200% text zoom has no clipped text.
4. **Performance:** production bundle JS ≤ 300 kB gzip total; first load on a mid phone
   (Playwright CPU throttle 4×, `Slow 4G` not needed: offline-first) shows the path in < 2 s.
5. **Black-box security attack** (Opus session, STANDARDS §8) against the e2e build:
   malicious backups (prototype pollution, oversized, deep nesting 10 000 levels, invalid UTF-8,
   huge numbers, wrong types), hash-route injection (`#/lesson/<script>`, `#/lesson/../../`,
   very long hashes), framing (load inside an iframe → frame-busting), CSP violations (try to
   `eval` from the console: blocked), service worker scope, no network requests other than own
   origin (Playwright `page.on('request')` assertion across a full lesson).
6. **Code review pass** (Opus, `/code-review high`) over the whole codebase, then fix.
7. **Full re-run** after all fixes: clean-room `rm -rf node_modules dist dist-e2e && npm ci &&
   npm run verify`, plus the screenshot visual QA again (AI changes cause side effects).
8. **Owner phone test** (give the owner this checklist in plain words):
   - install on iPhone (Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen) and/or Android;
   - play the first 3 lessons with sound on; flip the silent switch; mute in the app;
   - put the phone in airplane mode and play a lesson (works offline);
   - save a backup; check it appears in Files;
   - note anything confusing, too hard, too easy, ugly, or broken.
9. Fix what the owner reports (product changes → ask first / Opus planning session).
10. Final HANDOFF: "Live", how to update, how to back up, known limitations, ideas for later
    (PLAN §7).

## Acceptance
- All mutation checks recorded as "failed as expected".
- Both review passes resolved; clean-room verify green; owner signs off after the phone test.
